narrative.overview:
Devis is a heads-up review console. Smoked blue-black glass panes hover over a lit ink field, and light marks what the machine is attending to: the open pull request, the focused control, a running pipeline. The desk metaphor still holds: the queue sits on the left, the open pull request reads on the right, and commands stay in a frosted head above the content. Only the material changed. Everything floats; the small chrome that opens over content is frosted.

The glass is restrained, because the content is code. Panes carry a smoked tint and a luminous hairline edge; rows, cards and badges inside them do not. Blur is spent only on small sticky and floating chrome. One emissive cyan is the only brand color, and it glows only where it signals state. Diffs, findings, severity and comments keep their own colors and stay the loudest things on screen.

In the desktop shell, a Windows 11 Mica backdrop (22H2 and later) tints the field with the desktop wallpaper, and the app forces the dark theme so the glass always reads as smoked. Mica samples the wallpaper once, so it costs nothing per frame; `ADO_PR_OPS_BACKDROP=acrylic` opts back into the live acrylic blur, and `none` turns the backdrop off. Without a backdrop, the same field renders on solid ink.

The living reference is `web/design-system.html`. It renders the real `web/style.css`, so open it from the preview server to check any component. It is excluded from the packaged app.
keyCharacteristics: Floating glass panes separated by 8px gutters of lit field, never edge-to-edge chrome.
A cyan light pool top-left and an indigo pool bottom-right, with a faint 32px HUD grid fading out from the top-left.
Luminous hairline edges with a brighter top edge and an inner top sheen, so every pane catches light from above.
One emissive cyan, with glow reserved for selection, focus, running state and the primary command.
Cascadia Mono for every readout: IDs, branches, paths, build numbers and zoom levels.
One authored motion: an opened pull request resolves into the pane out of blur.

rules.name: The One Light Rule
rules.body: Only cyan glows. If two unrelated things on screen are cyan, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Color Is Evidence Rule
rules.body: Hue appears only where it carries meaning: a vote, a status, a severity or a diff line. Glass, edges and text stay cool and neutral.

rules.name: The Readout Rule
rules.body: Anything a machine produced and a person compares (an ID, a branch, a build number, a duration, a zoom level) is set in Cascadia Mono with tabular figures.

rules.name: The Glass Budget Rule
rules.body: Glass (tint plus edge) belongs only to panes, heads, floats, dialogs and pipeline blocks. Blur belongs only to the detail head, floats, dialogs and the zoom cluster: never to a pane, a sheet or anything repeated (`scripts/perf-guard-harness.mjs` enforces this). Rows, cards, badges and fields inside a pane are tints, never their own glass.

rules.name: The Near-Opaque Float Rule
rules.body: Anything that opens over content (heads, flyouts, menus, dialogs) is at least 84% opaque. Menus inside the frosted detail head can't blur the content under them, so their opacity is what keeps them legible.

rules.name: The Fallback Rule
rules.body: Glass must degrade to something solid and clear. Under `prefers-reduced-transparency`, the glass tokens turn opaque, blur is off, the HUD grid is hidden and the field is plain ink. In forced-colors mode, blur, the field effects and pane shadows are removed and system colors take over. Without a window backdrop, the field renders on solid ink.

dos: Do use the tokens; add a token before adding a raw value.
Do keep glass to panes, heads, floats, dialogs and pipeline blocks, and keep everything inside a pane as tints.
Do keep one emissive cyan per view, and let severity and diff colors carry meaning.
Do set IDs, branches, build numbers and other readouts in Cascadia Mono.
Do check new components in `web/design-system.html`, at 1440px and below 1100px, and with reduced transparency on.
donts: Don't make rows, cards, badges or fields their own glass; nested blur muddies the content and costs frames.
Don't let anything other than cyan glow, and don't glow decoratively: glow means selection, focus, running or the primary command.
Don't drop a float, head or dialog below 84% opacity; code and diagrams must never ghost through.
Don't add light-theme surfaces; the shell forces dark so the glass always reads as smoked.
Don't use colored side stripes on blocks, rows or cards.
Don't use emoji as icons; use `icon()` from `web/src/icons.ts`.
Don't put a `<button>` on the page without a base class.
Don't show raw HTML or Markdown in previews.
